reviewer: model visual review of the rendered block layout
authority: none - review artifact only; output.json remains authoritative
verdict: not yet spatially coherent - the payload cannot reach the platform, and the crank blocks the only service opening

checks.user_reachability: pass - input_member renders outside the shell on the front face with its swept disc clear of the housing wall
checks.swept_volume_conflicts: concern - transmission_shaft's disc overlaps the travelling_member prism in the cutaway; they have no declared interface
checks.assembly_feasibility: pass - the cover renders last on the front face and no piece is drawn behind it

findings.concern: The payload region renders OUTSIDE the shell while the platform that must carry it renders inside the core. The only boundary crossings are the crank and the service cover, so there is no opening through which a payload reaches the platform. As drawn, the product cannot be loaded.
findings.why_the_json_missed_it: The blueprint records payload_region as external and working_volume as core, each individually reasonable. It never asks whether the payload can reach the element that lifts it - there is no load-path-to-access check.
findings.missing_information: Stage 03 declares a payload region and an enclosure but never an access opening connecting the payload to the moving platform. A CLEARANCE or USER_ACCESS obligation on the travelling member is absent.

findings.concern: The service cover spans the front face and the crank sits directly outside its centre. The cover cannot be removed without removing the crank first, yet the crank is installed last in the assembly sequence.
findings.why_the_json_missed_it: The blueprint does flag this as access_blocked, but only the picture shows the crank is centred on the cover rather than beside it, and that the assembly order therefore reverses.
findings.missing_information: external pieces and boundary openings are both placed on the same nominal face with no lateral offset expressed

findings.concern: The travelling member is guided on one side only. guide_member renders as a single slab to the left of the platform with nothing opposing it. An eccentric payload would cock the platform about the screw.
findings.why_the_json_missed_it: The architecture declares one guide_member element and the blueprint faithfully places one. The JSON has no notion of a balanced or opposed pair, so a single guide reads as satisfied guidance.
findings.missing_information: the mechanism catalogue declares guidance as one element; it does not express that guidance against an eccentric load requires opposed supports

findings.concern: thrust_support renders at the top end and input_support at the bottom end, but both belong to the single support_region, which itself renders only at the bottom. Piece placement and region placement disagree.
findings.why_the_json_missed_it: Both obligations map to zone END. END is one zone used for two opposite ends, so the renderer had to choose, and its choice contradicts the region it belongs to.
findings.missing_information: END does not distinguish near from far along the primary axis, so two supports at opposite ends are indistinguishable in the blueprint

confirmed_from_blueprint: transmission_shaft rotates with no radial_support obligation (unsupported_span) - visible as a green block spanning the core with no red support touching it
10 unresolved interference candidates concentrated in the core column - visible as heavily overlapping blocks in the cutaway
